(a) prologue dead-store commit timing for the shared sl=1/r9=1 (count=1/redraw=1) constant: count, result, and redraw are assigned as ordinary statements (count=1; result=0; redraw=1;) right after object=Runtime_GetObject(actor), not as declaration initializers -- this reproduces the reference's single shared `movs r1,#1` being committed to sl (count) then r9 (redraw) immediately before r1 is reused for win1's UiWindow_CreateFar argument.
(b) the `flags = *(u16*)(object+216+selection*2) & 0x1ff` halfword load: splitting the byte offset into its own statement (`off = selection*2+216; flags = *(u16*)(object+off) & 0x1ff;`) keeps object untouched in its own register through to the load, which folds to a single reg+reg `ldrh r3,[r1,r3]` -- any single-expression algebraic regrouping of the same arithmetic (tried extensively in the prior round and again here) instead always materializes object+offset into one register first (`adds`+`adds`+`ldrh [r,#0]`).
(c) the `selection -1/+1 + count` wraparound adjustment: writing the -1/+1 as its own statement before the Modulo call (`selection -= 1; selection = Modulo(selection + count, count);`), matching sibling main:080b211c's exact idiom, commits the +-1 into selection's home register (r7) ahead of the add; folding it into a single `selection +- 1 + count` expression instead applies the +-1 to the sum register after the add -- a different, non-matching instruction order.
No PERM_GENERAL search was needed in the end; each of the three clusters was resolved by a targeted, evidence-backed statement-splitting/reordering edit matching either the sibling's idiom (a, c) or the reference's register-liveness shape (b), verified individually and then together.
